title: Hash Tables with Chaining
summary: The classic hash table - an array of buckets, each holding a chain of entries, insert, find and erase, the load factor and why the expected chain length stays constant, rehashing by doubling, how std::unordered_map is built and its bucket interface, reserve and max_load_factor, and the worst case.

cards.q: A chained hash table has 1,000 buckets and 3,000 entries, with a good hash. What is the expected chain length?
Why does every entry move to a different bucket (in general) during a rehash?
cards.a:
The bucket is hash % bucketCount, and the count changed

The hash stays the same, but taking it modulo a new count gives a new bucket.

cards.q: Why does doubling the buckets when the table is full keep insert at amortised O(1)?
cards.a:
All the rehashes together cost O(n)

Each rehash costs O(n), but they happen at sizes 8, 16, 32, ..., which sum to less than 2n, like a growing vector.
